newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent holds gains in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent holds gains in choppy trade.

text.p: IPE Brent held onto early gains on Wednesday amid support from bullish U.S. stock data, despite weaker NYMEX values, traders said.
Front month May Brent was five cents up at $20.30 a barrel by 1643 GMT after touching a high of $20.47 and dipping to a low of $20.21.
April gas oil futures were $2.25 higher at $174.25 a tonne. WTI April was 11 cents adrift at $21.95 a barrel.
"We are just holding onto yesterday's gains and technically we're still looking good," a trader said.
"People are looking for gasoline to give some follow through strength from yesterday but there's really not a lot lof trade going on and it hasn't fed through into gains."
Other traders forecast volatility ahead of the expiry of April NYMEX crude on Thursday and reported caution about possible spikes in the U.S. gasoline market.
The May/June spread was steady at around 16 cents.
Despite the consolidation moves there had been some technical buying and players were getting a little more positive about the market.
Some of the short-term hedge funds would probably find the confidence to come in and buy the market now that it has popped above the $20 mark, one trader said.
"People are just squaring up after the big move yesterday and having another fresh look at it," said another trader. "It's deadly quiet, there's no news."
